decisions.executionNote: Begin left-tube approach with a rising elbow-up arc; right arm stays home. Tube location and yaw estimated from RGB.
Advance over the left tube while rotating the open gripper toward a downward grasp aligned with its axis.
Finish aligning over the left tube and descend cautiously; refine grasp from the next wrist view.
Lower the last 16 mm and close on the centered left tube. Retention will be checked during lift.
Lift the grasped left tube clear with the gripper commanded closed; preserve elbow-up configuration.
Carry the retained tube inward while gradually turning it upright, keeping clearance above the table.
Continue smooth rotation toward upright while moving above a left-side rack opening; keep holding closed.
Finish bringing the tube upright above the leftmost large front opening, before lowering into the rack.
Lower toward the selected left rack hole with a small lateral correction; inspect alignment before the final insertion.
Insert the upright left tube slowly along the slot axis, keeping its lateral position fixed.
Release at the rack and withdraw gently to inspect whether the first tube has settled upright into its opening.
The released tube appears tipped rather than seated. Back away for an unobstructed recovery view.
Clear the head view of the tipped tube to determine a safe recovery grasp, without touching the rack.
Approach the tube resting across the left rack edge from above, rotating to align the open fingers for recovery.
Continue the overhead recovery approach with gradual wrist rotation and elbow-up continuity.
Align the downward open grasp with the tube lying across the rack; stop above it for wrist-camera correction.
Replan after continuity rejection with much smaller increments, lowering gently toward the displaced tube rather than advancing the rejected target.
Relieve contact, center the fingers on the tube body from the wrist view, and attempt a recovery grip without further downward pushing.
Avoid the rejected forward/upward direction. Close at the current tube-body height, then withdraw toward the left workspace to test retention.
The tube appears between the fingers after recovery. Withdraw from the rack while rotating its cap upward, keeping the closed grip.
The recovered tube was not retained. Clear the left arm while beginning an elbow-up approach to the undisturbed near-right tube.
Continue right-tube alignment along its cap-to-tip axis while the left arm withdraws and unwinds.
Finish the downward approach above the near-right tube, leaving clearance for visual refinement.
Refine right tube yaw and centering from the wrist view, descend the final 28 mm, and close for pickup.
Allow the right gripper to close fully, then lift the tube clear to verify retention.
Carry the retained right tube inward above the table and begin turning it upright for a right-side rack slot.
Continue the elevated inward transfer and gradual upright rotation, holding the tube closed.
Bring the held tube over the rack's right side, then inspect its actual axis and slot alignment before insertion.
Move the upright tube toward the rightmost large opening and lower to an inspection height, keeping orientation fixed.
Lower vertically in small increments to inspect tube-to-slot alignment while maintaining the closed grasp.
The tube appears to have contacted the rack surface. Lift clear and shift toward the front row before retrying, rather than pushing downward.
Retry the right-front slot with a straight, slow descent after correcting the row alignment.
Relieve the rim contact and make an 8 mm inward/backward alignment correction before a short insertion test.
Release the supported upright tube and withdraw gently to check whether it settles into the opening without gripper interference.
The released right tube appears upright in an opening. Withdraw the right arm and approach the central loose tube with the left arm, staying on its side.
The released tube fell out, so insertion is not confirmed. Continue the central-tube pickup and clear the right arm for a later recovery.
Align the left gripper above the central tube while keeping the EE on the left side of the workspace.
Center the left fingers on the tube with a slight wrist tilt while staying left of the midline, then close at pickup height.
Finish closing, then lift the central tube clear of the table for a measured upright alignment with a large rack opening.
Rotate the retained tube upright while moving toward the left front large slot, maintaining clearance and a closed grip.
Continue the smooth upright rotation and leftward transfer; hold above the rack before final visual alignment.
Finish making the tube upright and pause above the rack to refine its axis against the chosen large opening.
Align the upright tube with the clearly visible central large front opening using the calibrated head view; retain vertical clearance.
Lower the aligned tube 30 mm toward the central large opening, with a small rightward axis correction.
Continue the vertical insertion test slowly, watching for tube motion relative to the fingers rather than assuming seating.
The tube remains fixed in the fingers during descent. Continue toward seating depth without changing its lateral alignment.
Tube motion indicates rim contact rather than insertion. Lift to unload it and correct the depth-plane alignment rearward before retrying.
Test the corrected central-slot alignment with a slow vertical descent; keep the tube closed until seating is visually supported.
The tube stayed fixed relative to the fingers while descending. Continue deeper into the opening to account for the lower grasp point after prior sliding.
Unload the rim and move the tube toward the large opening visible just in front of its tip in the wrist view; avoid continued downward contact.
Refine centering on the large visible hole with a small rightward/frontward shift, unloading contact before lateral motion.
